method: Direct fetch of Cohere's and University of Waterloo's own announcement pages (both dated 6 August 2026), cross-checked for consistency, plus a targeted web search for criticism, dispute, delay, or cancellation. Given a short cycle window, this cycle combined the verifier and falsifier roles rather than using two separate sub-agent contexts; risk was judged low because both primaries are the two announcing parties themselves and no third party's account needed reconciling.
origin_items: Found via cycle-1 Tier-0 sweep of Cohere Blog; dedup-checked (strong match against cohere-university-of-toronto-partnership, ruled coincidental in cycle 2); carried to cycle 4 for verification.

claims.text: On 6 August 2026, Cohere and the University of Waterloo announced a partnership under which Waterloo's Future of Work Institute will develop a non-credit 'AI Transformation and Change Management' certificate, launching in fall 2026, covering AI literacy, human-centered design, ethics, business strategy, and change management
claims.reasoning: Both parties' own pages state this consistently. No independent (non-reprint) third-party outlet coverage found via search as of verification time.

claims.text: The first cohort is scheduled to start in January 2027, with 20 co-op positions dedicated to structured AI-transformation work with private, public-sector, and non-profit organizations, open to students from any faculty
claims.reasoning: Direct quote from University of Waterloo's own page; Cohere's blog does not repeat the January 2027 detail but does not contradict it either.

claims.text: Cohere Chief AI Officer Joelle Pineau said Waterloo 'has played a defining role' in building Canada's AI talent pipeline; Future of Work Institute executive director Edith Law said 'AI adoption is not the point, but solving problems is'
claims.reasoning: Direct attributed quotes on University of Waterloo's own page.

falsifier_notes: Search for criticism/dispute/delay/cancellation of the partnership returned nothing beyond the two primary announcement pages and unrelated Cohere news (Bell, Quebec government partnerships). Dedup gate returned exit 2 (strong, score 0.8) against cohere-university-of-toronto-partnership on title-template similarity alone (zero shared source URLs, unrelated universities and programs) -- read in full in cycle 2 and judged coincidental, not a duplicate or follow-up, satisfying verification.md 0a's requirement to justify outcome (c) against a strong match. No dollar figure disclosed by either party.
